claims.text: ScholAR provides a local-first scientific paper assistant with inspectable text and visual evidence.
The ingestion pipeline preserves source identity across PDF, AST, page, chunk, figure, and SQLite artifacts.
Strict-local network policy blocks remote calls and allows local loopback model engines like Ollama.
The verifier performs deterministic lexical checking and citation remapping rather than semantic entailment.
The full question-answering workflow records an inspectable answer trace and evidence graph.
Retrospective retrieval: BM25+dense RRF reaches Hit@1 of 0.85 versus 0.84 for BM25 with overlapping CI, while modality boosting drops Hit@1 to 0.59.
Deterministic repair increases lexical overlap F1 from 0.159 to 0.224 but decreases cited-page alignment from 0.670 to 0.618.
Paired pipeline abstained status declines from 13 to 5 cases across 20 cross-paper controls after repair.
Stratified 50-question human evaluation protocol with 5 raters; results gated pending completion of collection.

LLM-based evaluation covering the 150-case complement: 52.2% correctness on eligible references (n=113), 74.7% evidence grounding, and 73.3% citation accuracy; these are model judgments rather than human ratings, and the later out-of-schema visual labels are excluded.
